credit_line: perpetuating the family's legacy in the world of music
story: Jean-Henri Naderman built single-action harps in Paris around 1780. In 1778, he was appointed royal harp maker to Queen Marie-Antoinette, whose passion for the instrument turned it into a major fashion across Parisian salons. Naderman built and refined harps for the royal court and operated a music publishing business to support the repertoire. His son François-Joseph pursued a celebrated career as a harpist, eventually joining his brother Henri as a professor at the Paris Conservatoire.
